review_notes: I read the helper kits (BC, Scal, Ord, Conj, PKit, S3GlueKit, C3Kit, kitW) and the main `solution` proof body. I did not examine the huge hypothesis block in detail. I checked the definitions of `scalePoly` and `substPoly` and Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.map_aeval`. I did not check whether the proposed lemmas would compile. A possible fourth duplicate is the `hμ*`/`hTpow` induction pattern, which I did not pursue. I only compared `hWpow` and `hattpow` loosely.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out several times: iterate a map that preserves a predicate p, then use μ^n = 1 to get back from p (μ x) to p x via (μ^(n-1)) (μ x) = x. It appears for p = (· ∈ B) (hμmB, lines 1124-1127). It appears for the 'in B and in maximal ideal' predicate (hμmP, 1128-1137, with the inverse step in hμP', 1139-1145). It appears for p = (· ∈ W) (the inner induction at 1155-1159 and the final `rwa` at 1160). `solution` then repeats the iff-version for Wt as `hWpow` (1652-1656). Each copy redoes the `pow_succ`/`AlgEquiv.mul_apply` rewriting and the `Nat.sub_add_cancel hn, hμn, AlgEquiv.one_apply` step. The hμmP and hμP' copies also redo the dependent `Subtype.ext` bookkeeping.
findings.proposed_change: Add one generic lemma, e.g. `theorem pow_apply_of_forall {K} [Field K] {k} [Field k] [Algebra k K] (μ : K ≃ₐ[k] K) (p : K → Prop) (hp : ∀ x, p x → p (μ x)) : ∀ m x, p x → p ((μ ^ m) x)`. The proof is induction on m with `pow_succ` and `AlgEquiv.mul_apply`. Add a companion `theorem of_apply_of_pow_eq_one ... (hn : 0 < n) (hμn : μ ^ n = 1) (hp) : p (μ x) → p x`. It applies the first lemma to `μ x` with m = n-1 and rewrites `(μ ^ (n-1)) (μ x) = x` once. For the maximal-ideal part, take `p x := ∃ hx : x ∈ B, (⟨x, hBW x hx⟩ : W) ∈ maximalIdeal W`, so hμmP and hμP' become one-line instances. The W-membership induction and final `rwa` also become one-line instances. Add an iff variant, `(∀ x, p x ↔ p (μ x)) → ∀ m x, p x ↔ p ((μ^m) x)`, which gives `hWpow` directly with `hτ₀W`. `mem_iff_map_mem_of_pow_eq_one` then only keeps the `fwd` step that uses `hloc`.
findings.benefit: This removes about five hand-rolled inductions and two copies of the inverse-step calculation. It makes explicit that the argument is generic iteration of a self-map, and it avoids dependent-subtype casts in the maximal-ideal case. Future changes to the hypotheses of `mem_iff_map_mem_of_pow_eq_one` then touch one lemma instead of several.

findings.problem: The two theorems have identical proof skeletons. Each builds `h : (MvPolynomial.map e).comp φ₀.toRingHom = φ.toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.map e)`, applies `ringHom_ext`, and proves the constant case with the same `simp only [... MvPolynomial.algHom_C, MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq, MvPolynomial.map_C]`. Each then closes with the same `congrArg (fun φ : ... => φ f) h`. Only the variable case differs. Both `scalePoly` and `substPoly` are defined as `aeval` of a family of polynomials, so the common step is 'map commutes with aeval of a family'.
findings.proposed_change: State one lemma: for e : κ₀ →+* κ and families s₀ : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) κ₀ and s : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) κ with `∀ i, map e (s₀ i) = s i`, we have `map e (aeval s₀ f) = aeval s (map e f)`. Prove it by `ringHom_ext` once, or by `MvPolynomial.map_aeval` from Mathlib (`φ (aeval g p) = eval₂Hom (φ.comp (algebraMap R S₁)) (fun i => φ (g i)) p`) plus `aeval` unfolding. Then `map_scalePoly` is the instance with s₀ i = C c * X i, whose image under map e is C (e c) * X i. `map_substPoly` is the instance with s₀ j = ∑ i, C (ofZMod (g i j)) * X i and `map_sum`, `map_mul`, `e_ofZMod`. The same lemma could serve any future base-change compatibility of an `aeval`-defined action.
findings.benefit: This removes about 20 duplicated tactic lines. It makes the proof reflect the fact that both maps are `aeval`s, so `bc_hAction` reduces to checking two small identities on generators. It avoids the unwieldy `simp only` lists that break when the definitions change.

findings.excerpt: have hmem₁ : ((1 : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod q)), cu) ∈ DrinfeldCurve.hSubgroup q := by
findings.problem: The same piece of reasoning is repeated inside `solution` for γ₀ (1623-1627), for γ₀^k (1662-1666), and partly for γ*γσ (1838-1842, 1850-1855). From γ ∈ Gamma q and (redQ q γ, c) ∈ hSubgroup q, it (i) rewrites `redQ q γ = 1` with `hredΓ` to get (1, c) ∈ hSubgroup, (ii) packages c as an element of `rootsOfUnity (q+1)` via `Scal.mem_rootsOfUnity_of_one_mem`, and (iii) proves `⟨(redQ q γ, c), hmem⟩ = sc q c'` by `Subtype.ext (Prod.ext (hredΓ ..) rfl)`. The ck case then writes out `⟨ck, mem_rootsOfUnity_of_one_mem q ck hmemk1⟩` twice, in `hsck` and in the `refine`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma next to `Scal.sc_mk_eq`, e.g. `theorem Scal.exists_sc_eq_of_redQ_eq_one (γ : SL(2,ℤ)) (hγ : redQ q γ = 1) (c : (GaloisField q 2)ˣ) (hmem : (redQ q γ, c) ∈ hSubgroup q) : ∃ c' : rootsOfUnity (q+1) (GaloisField q 2), (c' : (GaloisField q 2)ˣ) = c ∧ (⟨(redQ q γ, c), hmem⟩ : hSubgroup q) = sc q c'`. Its proof is `hγ ▸ ...` using `mem_rootsOfUnity_of_one_mem` and `Subtype.ext (Prod.ext hγ rfl)`. Prove `hredΓ` once as a lemma, since the third copy (`hredμ`) unfolds `redQ` by hand again. Then c₀ and ck are obtained by `obtain ⟨c₀, rfl, hsc₀⟩ := exists_sc_eq_of_redQ_eq_one ...` for γ₀ and γ₀^k. In the cμ' case the lemma applies to the term `γσ` (the part in Gamma q) and the multiplicativity argument of `hsplit` remains.
findings.benefit: This removes repeated subtype-packaging boilerplate from a very long proof. It names the fact that elements of hSubgroup with trivial matrix part are exactly the `sc` images, which is what the `Ord` and `Conj` lemmas consume. It also makes the three uses uniform and reduces the risk of the casts diverging.
